candidates.name: Town Hall
candidates.content: The Town Hall is the centrepiece of the Rynek. It was built in the Gothic style in the first years of the 14th century. It was later rebuilt in Renaissance style by Giovanni Battista di Quadro from Lugano. It is said to be the mos

candidates.name: Archaeological Museum
candidates.content: With 42,432 artifacts, this is a large and fascinating museum. It specializes in the archeology of Wielkopolska and Egypt. Located in the Gorka Palace built by influential magnate family in mid-15h century, rebuilt in 16th century

candidates.name: The Museum of Poznań Uprising 1956
candidates.price: 8 zł, 4 zł reduced, free on Tu
candidates.content: Placed in the interiors of Emperor's Castle shows exhibits connected with the Poznań workers' protest against the communist system in June 1956. On the exhibition there are photos of attendants and their personal belongings, and h

candidates.name: Fort VII
candidates.price: 6 zł entrance, Tu free; 70 zł guide
candidates.content: One of several forts located around Poznań, this one is quite infamous as it became concentration camp during Second World War with the purpose to purge undesirables (Jews and local elite). Later it became only transient concentra

candidates.name: Stary Rynek
candidates.content: The old town square, one of the finest in Europe. This is the centre of old, medieval Poznań, and has been superbly rebuilt after severe destruction in World War II. Cafés and bars line the square and it is a superb spot for order

candidates.name: The former Jesuits' College
candidates.content: It was an old Jesuits' school build by the monk in the same period, as the neighboring church, now houses the City Office - so it's possible to get in to see the interiors, but only halls and corridors. In the early 19th century i

candidates.name: King's Castle
candidates.content: The King's Castle (Zamek Królewski) - rebuilt by King Przemysł II in 1290s, but erected by his father, Duke Przemysł I as a duke's residence for Poznań county. The only remnants of the original building are the foundations, and -

candidates.name: Museum of Applied Arts
candidates.content: Displays crafts, furniture, precious metals and glassware.

candidates.name: The Holy Blood of Lord Jesus Church
candidates.content: The church's erection is connected with a legend about desecration of the host done by a group of Jews. During services the priest stands backward to the people, and the church is used both by Roman Catholics and Greek Catholics (

candidates.name: Imperial Castle
candidates.content: Erected 1905-1910 by Franz Schwechten, the Berlin court architect of German emperor Wilhelm II. The huge neo-Romanesque building, which alludes to medieval constructions, was officially opened by the Emperor. It was the seat of Po

candidates.name: Stary Marych
candidates.content: A very unusual monument os. Stary Marych, at the very beginning of Półwiejska Str. (a shopping pedestrian zone), which is probably the only monument in the world of a man walking with a bike (all other cyclers ride). The Monumemo

candidates.name: St. Peter's and Paul's Cathedral
candidates.alt: Bazylika archikatedralna Świętych Apostołów Piotra i Pawła
candidates.content: St. Peter's and Paul's Cathedral was the first Polish cathedral and is a burial place of 8 Polish dukes and kings from the Piast dynasty including the famous Mieszko I and his son Bolesław the Brave. It was a probable baptism plac

candidates.name: Archbishopric Museum
candidates.content: Placed in the former Lubrański Academy - the second oldest (after Kraków) higher school in Poland founded by bishop John Lubrański in 1518. The exhibition shows church art, mostly from the Greater Poland region, from early Middle

candidates.name: Brama Poznania ICHOT
candidates.content: History of Cathedral Island, and the establishment of Poznań. Audioguide and interactive exhibits throughout the tour, and a nice rooftop view.

candidates.name: St. Margaret Church
candidates.content: A late-Romanesque church (with some Gothic features) in the middle of Środka Market Square, nowadays a side-church for the cathedral parish. It is hard to get inside, unless you come approx. a quarter before or after services.

candidates.name: Church of St. John of Jerusalem
candidates.content: The first building on Polish territories built with bricks (before only wooden or stone building were erected) around the year 1188. The church was erected for the Johnnites order, who were running a hospital for the poor people n

candidates.name: Museum of Poznań
candidates.content: In beautiful and original (not damaged during World War II) interiors of Poznań Town Hall, shows objects and documents from the whole city history since the 10th century.

candidates.name: Museum of Musical Instruments
candidates.content: With 2000 items from all over the world, this is the only exhibition of its kind in Poland. It also has an extensive collection of Chopin memorabilia.

candidates.name: The Archbishop's Palace
candidates.content: The palace was built at the same time as the cathedral, but its present shape comes from the 2nd half of 18th century. It is closed to visitors.

candidates.name: Motoring Museum
candidates.content: Run by the Wielkopolska Motoring Club, features a range of vintage and notable vehicles.

candidates.name: The models of Old Poznan
candidates.content: Main model representing Poznań is a 30-minutes recap of Poznań history from its founding at the turn of 9th and 10th century till 18th century. Another model presents the beginnings of the city and its crucial role played during t

candidates.name: Citadel Park
candidates.content: A fortress was built here by the Prussians in 1828; it was destroyed during fighting in 1945. It contains a cemetery for the Russian, Polish and British soldiers who lost their lives here.

candidates.name: Morasko Meteorite Nature Reserve
candidates.content: The nature reservation "The Morasko Meteorite” – one of only two places like that in Europe (the second one is in Estonia) – a system of 7 craters left after a meteorite fall several thousands years ago. The name ‘Morasko’ comes f

candidates.name: The City Church of St. Stanislaus and Our Lady
candidates.hours: 06:00-19:30 daily, no visits during mass service
candidates.content: This church was reopened in 2007 after total refurbishment, one of the most beautiful baroque churches in Poland. It was built as a Jesuits' church; it is now the parish church for the Old Town. Many tourist come here for the soun

candidates.name: The Franciscan Church
candidates.content: It is a rather typical church from the turn of 17th and 18th centuries​, but is really worth coming here at least for a few minutes for its beautiful paintings on the vaulting and wood carvings created by two ingenious monk - brot

candidates.name: The Our Lady Church
candidates.content: Our Lady Church was built in late Gothic style (approx. 1430), not very significant for its present shape and values, but important for its role in the 10th century, when in the place the duke's palace and a small chapel were buil

candidates.name: Psalter House
candidates.content: It was erected in the beginnings of 16th century​ (by Bishop Lubrański) as a rehearsal-place for psalter singers. They were due to sing the David's Psalms in the Cathedral the whole day round. It is now used by Christian associati

candidates.name: Literary Museum of Henryk Sienkiewicz
candidates.content: Sienkiewicz, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1905, is best known for his work Quo Vadis?, an epic on early Christians in the Roman empire. He is Poland's most celebrated novelist, and this is the most extensive collectio

candidates.name: Termy Maltańskie
candidates.hours: all zones open before 12:00, all close on 23:00
candidates.content: One of the largest aquaparks in Poland with large sports swimming pool and saunas (all three are separate zones paid and visited separately). Many water slides, wave pool and other attractions. Outdoor swimming pools are available

candidates.name: Nowe Zoo
candidates.price: over 45 zł in season (Mar-Oct), 15 zł off-season (Nov-Feb)
candidates.content: Huge zoo for a casual stroll located in a forest, large variety of animals (including elephants, tigers, seals and bisons) on spacious enclosures. Long distances may be a bit boring or tough on children. Zoo became popular for its

candidates.name: KKS Lech Poznań
candidates.content: "The railwaymen" play soccer in Ekstraklasa, the top tier. KKS stands for Kolejowy Klub Sportowy, railway sports club, and a splendid Ty 51 steam locomotive stands in front of the stadium. Stadion Miejski is now sponsored as Enea

candidates.name: Rusałka Lake
candidates.content: Small artificial lake with a beach and a little culinary infrastructure and a pedalo rental. Nice green scenery and many paths around lake. Disturbing fact worth noting is that lake was built during Second World War using forced l

candidates.name: Strzeszyn Lake
candidates.content: Located further from centre, beach around this lake is a bit more spacious than near Rusałka. There are some restaurants, large children playground, a field to set up barbecue and a pedalo rental.

candidates.name: Kiekrz Lake
candidates.content: Large, open lake located quite far off centre but still within city limits. Not much infrastructure for casual swimmers as this place is catering more for those wishing to swim on a boat, fish or do water sports like windsurfing.

candidates.name: Park Railway Maltanka
candidates.content: Park train which goes from city to the zoo close to Malta Lake. Source of amusement for many children who ride it. Some rides are completed using steam train.

candidates.name: Malta Lake
candidates.content: Long artificial lake with rowing track used in professional competitions. There is about 5km long path going around entire lake often used for marathon runs. Small swimming spot and leisure centre with huge children playground are

candidates.name: Namesday of St. Martin street
candidates.content: On 11th November parade happens on Święty Marcin street. Various colorful acts including legionnary Martin on a horse, Bamberg girl and personified goose march from St. Martin church to Imperial Castle where various concerts happe

candidates.name: Malta Ski
candidates.hours: 10:00-20:00 daily, may close earlier in bad weather
candidates.content: Small year-round dry ski slope. Training available. There is also a tobbogan run, carousel, mini-golf and children driving town.

candidates.name: Klub 'Pod Minogą'
candidates.content: Music club mostly catering to small, cosy concerts (usually rock), good acoustics that does not hurt ears too much. Climate of old 90s bar with raw brick walls, old wood and delicate humid stench.

candidates.name: Kultowa
candidates.content: Go to pub with lots of smoke for a slower day. Brick, cosy interiors and 80s/90s Polish rock hits.

candidates.name: KontenerART
candidates.content: Chill location near river to drink a few beers and have a dance or two. Good for small groups or singles.

candidates.name: Cuba Libre
candidates.content: Latin music, most nights the owner gives a basic salsa-lesson early at night, before that Latin Parties with different DJs and music.

candidates.name: Pierogarnia Stary Młyn
candidates.content: Traditional Polish food restaurant with rustic interiors. Wide variety of pierogi, including sour, sweet, meat and vegan options. Bigos and żurek are also available.

candidates.name: Ratuszova
candidates.content: Traditional and modern Polish food arranged very elegantly. Beautiful location on the Market. Has outside serving, the inside is several unique smaller rooms in old charming building.

candidates.name: Avanti
candidates.content: For those on low budget, this is an inexpensive fast-serve place with few kinds of spaghetti or lasagne. Served almost immediately: pasta and sauce are always ready. (Tip: go for carbonara pasta).

candidates.name: Piccolo
candidates.content: Small selection of spaghetti and lasagne on very tight budget. There are several of them within the city; one of the most useful is on Rynkowa 1 only few steps from the Old Market Sq.

candidates.name: Dramat
candidates.content: A cheap place on the Rynek serving Polish food. Perennially popular.

candidates.name: Bar Pod Arkadami
candidates.content: One of the last remaining milk bars in Poznań. A place to eat a meal on the cheap that is not spaghetti.

candidates.name: Kociak
candidates.content: Very famous for its wonderful desserts and milk shakes. Don't be astonished with the interiors: it is a cafe bar, not a luxurious café.

candidates.name: Kura Warzyw Gemüse Kebab
candidates.content: Posh döner kebab inspired by German originals. Higher quality than typical Polish kebab, but quite expensive. Vegan options available. Open till early morning.

candidates.name: Bamberka
candidates.content: In the middle of Old Market Square in the building of former Weigh House, Stary Rynek 2.

candidates.name: Wiejskie Jadło
candidates.content: A restaurant network stylized for a traditional old-polish peasant's house, located at the main square.

candidates.name: Double B's American Dinner
candidates.content: Restaurant based on popular image of American 50s restaurants. Serves burgers, hot-dogs and other American-inspired cuisine.

candidates.name: H.P. Cukiernia
candidates.content: One of the best places to get St. Martin's croissant in city centre. Expect long queues. They also sell other confectionery.

candidates.name: Jezycki Market
candidates.content: Mostly for the locals living in Jezyce district, a huge choice of meat, some flowers, vegetables, some clothes and shoes. Much better prices than in shops in the centre, but don't expect much English (or any other language). If yo

candidates.name: Posnania
candidates.content: Gigamall in eastern Poznań not too far off city centre. Main alley in the mall is about 700-metre trip. Huge selection of fashion and a variety of many other shops. Food court is located in main entrance close to tram stop. Superm

candidates.name: Łazarski Market
candidates.content: Also assigned mostly for locals, apart from food, flowers and clothes – some toys and electronic equipment.

candidates.name: Wielkopolski Square Market
candidates.content: Mostly flowers, vegetables-fruit and sweets, some meat.

candidates.name: Wildecki Market
candidates.content: A market similar to Jezycki Market

december.text: Important part of local history is Greater Polish uprising which happened right after Germany surrendered in First World War. It was a sweeping success which allowed Poles to end German occupation as great powers were unwilling to cede the province and Poznań to Poland at first. Arrival of Jan Paderewski to the city wh

The Christmas Market "The Poznań Bethleyem” – stalls with souvenirs, with Christmas decorations, hot wine, on the Old Market Square and nearby the west entrance to the Stary Browar Mall. Always three weeks before Christmas.
The Kid Films Festival 'Ale Kino' (‘What a Cinema’) – a festival of films produced for young watchers, yearly from 1983 in December.
